task:
Research PyTorch CUDA wheel architecture coverage to decide the right CUDA runtime version for a Docker TTS image that must run on NVIDIA GPUs from RTX 20 series (Turing sm_75) through RTX 50 series (Blackwell sm_120). Be precise and sourced.

Context: our image currently uses torch 2.11.0+cu126, whose shipped arch list is ['sm_50','sm_60','sm_70','sm_75','sm_80','sm_86','sm_90'] — NO sm_89, sm_100, or sm_120. RTX 40 works today only because sm_86 cubins are binary-compatible with sm_89. RTX 50 (sm_120) cannot run on cu126 at all.

Questions:

1. What is the exact TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST for the official PyTorch 2.11.0+cu128 Linux x86_64 wheel? Specifically: does it include sm_75 (Turing, RTX 20 series) and sm_120 (Blackwell, RTX 50)? Also does it include sm_89/sm_100? Check the pytorch/builder GitHub repo build configs for v2.11.0 / release/2.11 (files like manywheel/build.sh or .ci/... scripts) and any PyTorch 2.11 release notes about dropping or keeping Turing/Ampere archs.

2. Same question for torch 2.11.0+cu130 (or any cu130 torch build): does the cu130 build include sm_75? IMPORTANT: CUDA 13.0 may have dropped or deprecated Turing (sm_75) support — verify whether PyTorch cu130 wheels still ship sm_75 cubins, or whether moving to cu130 would lose RTX 20 series support. Also check whether CUDA 13.0 dropped sm_70 (Volta) and what that means for sm_75.

3. Minimum host NVIDIA driver required for: (a) CUDA 12.8 (torch cu128) — confirm >= 570.26 on Linux; (b) CUDA 13.0 (torch cu130) — what is the minimum driver (580.x?) on Linux? Cite NVIDIA CUDA release notes tables.

4. Does PyTorch 2.11.0+cu128 run on sm_75 (Turing) in practice — any known regressions/dropped Turing support in PyTorch 2.11? And does PyTorch 2.11+cu128 run on sm_120 (RTX 50) — any known issues (e.g. needing specific env vars like PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF, or cuDNN issues on Blackwell)?

5. torchaudio: does torchaudio 2.11.0 exist for cu128 and cu130 (matching torch 2.11.0)? Any version pairing constraints?

Return a concise factual summary with source URLs. Explicitly flag anything unverified.

criteriaSatisfied.evidence: All findings are concrete with exact file paths and severity. Q1/Q2 arch lists verified by installing the actual wheels (torch-2.11.0+cu128/cu130/cu126 cp311 Linux x86_64 from download.pytorch.org) and calling torch._C._cuda_getArchFlags(): cu128='sm_75 sm_80 sm_86 sm_90 sm_100 sm_120', cu130='sm_75 sm_80 sm_86 sm_90 sm_100 sm_120', cu126='sm_50 sm_60 sm_70 sm_75 sm_80 sm_86 sm_90'. Cross-checked against pytorch/pytorch@v2.11.0/.ci/manywheel/build_cuda.sh (lines 107-120) and RFC #172663 support matrix. Q3 driver minima from NVIDIA release notes Table 3: CUDA 12.8 GA >=570.26, 13.0 GA >=580.65.06. Q4 sm_120 issues cited by GitHub issue number (#179214 CTCLoss backward OOR, #181379 cuDNN SDPA head_dim<=128 on sm_120, #176426 Triton multi-tl.load segfault, #182286 allocator fragmentation). Q5 torchaudio 2.11.0+cu128/cu130 wheels confirmed to exist (cp310-cp313) with zero Requires-Dist (no hard torch pin).

validationOutput: Methodology validated: cu126 arch flags exactly reproduce the user's stated list ['sm_50','sm_60','sm_70','sm_75','sm_80','sm_86','sm_90']
cu128 vs cu130 arch lists are identical (sm_75 sm_80 sm_86 sm_90 sm_100 sm_120) - both cover RTX 20 (sm_75) through RTX 50 (sm_120)
Embedded nvcc gencode string in libtorch_cuda.so matches _cuda_getArchFlags() output byte-for-byte

cu128/cu130 wheels ship cuDNN 9.19.0.56 and depend on PyPI packages cuda-toolkit==12.8.1/13.0.2, cuda-bindings, nvidia-cudnn-cu12/cu13==9.19.0.56, nvidia-nccl-cu12/cu13==2.28.9, triton==3.6.0 (Docker build must install these)
residualRisks: cuDNN 9.19 Turing/Blackwell arch support is corroborated (PyTorch statements + shipped wheel composition + cuDNN SDPA acceptance range [sm_80,sm_121] per #181379) but NVIDIA's cuDNN support-matrix page is JS-only and could not be directly fetched

Deep fatbin parse (exact per-cubin arch enumeration) was not fully decoded (CUDA 12.x fatbin headers are non-ASCII/nonstandard); arch-flags API + gencode string + cubin-count consistency used instead - all three agree

sm_120 runtime issues (#179214 CTCLoss backward, #181379 cuDNN SDPA head_dim, #176426 Triton segfault, #182286 allocator fragmentation) are community-reported and open as of research date (2026-08-13); none block basic TTS inference but should be tracked

#183806 (linalg.eig/eigh 30-130x slower on 2.11+cu130) is aarch64/GH200-specific; the underlying MAGMA->cuSOLVER switch is a 2.11-wide behavior change worth a smoke test on the TTS pipeline (linalg.svd/solve_triangular/lstsq paths)
Driver minima cited from NVIDIA toolkit-driver tables; the practical runtime floor for CUDA 13.x is '>=580' per the minor-version-compatibility table
Windows driver rows for CUDA 13.0 are N/A (display driver unbundled); not relevant to Linux Docker image
childReport.diffSummary: Research-only task; no repository files changed. Artifacts in /tmp: downloaded wheels (torch 2.11.0 cu126/cu128/cu130 cp311+cp312), 3 verification venvs (torchvenv/torchvenv126/torchvenv130), extracted wheel libs, PR diff, release-notes HTML captures.
reviewFindings: info: cu128 and cu130 have identical arch coverage (sm_75..sm_120); cu130 is the recommended choice (stable PyPI variant; cu128 deprecated in PyTorch 2.12 per dev-discuss #3337)
info: cu126 (current image) covers sm_50..sm_90 only - cannot run RTX 50 (no sm_100/sm_120 cubins, no forward-compat PTX); user's premise confirmed
info: sm_89 never shipped in any PyTorch wheel; RTX 40 relies on sm_86->sm_89 binary compatibility (NVIDIA CUDA C Programming Guide 3.1.2)
warning: CUDA 13.0 dropped Maxwell/Pascal/Volta but NOT Turing; RTX 20 (sm_75) fully supported on cu130 - the 'cu130 loses RTX 20' fear is unfounded
warning: host driver must be >=580.65.06 (prefer >=580.95.05) for cu130 vs >=570.26 for cu128

warning: Blackwell-specific open issues (#179214 CTCLoss backward resource limits, #181379 cuDNN SDPA head_dim<=128 on sm_120, #176426 Triton JIT segfault, #182286 allocator fragmentation) - set PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True for RTX 50 images
info: torchaudio 2.11.0+cu128 and +cu130 both exist; no hard torch pin in METADATA; pair by matching version string
